newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mild, rain-free outlook for Brazil coffee - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Mild, rain-free outlook for Brazil coffee - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions should see temperatures pick up through the coming week, with rain-free forecasts pointing to favorable harvesting conditions, local meteorologists Somar said in an update Monday.

Minimum temperatures over the past 24 hours did not fall below 10 degrees Celsius throughout the coffee belt and winds from the north should mean temperatures will pick up throughout the week, it added.
Long-term models show a new cold front accompanied by a polar air mass should arrive in the south of the country during the weekend of July 12-13.

The center of the polar air mass is currently forecast to have an intensity of 1,032 millibars over Argentina which would mean around 1,020 millibars over southern Parana, said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
For the time being, the air mass is expected to pass through only the south of the country, prevented from rising into the coffee regions by the prevailing low pressure system, he added.
"Also it looks as if, if anything, the air mass will get weaker rather than stronger," Massari said.
